fix(test): a viewer read closes a viewer the restored session state left open (brandon-unfiled-3248.vfhf)

On Linux CI the SIGKILLed starter's last session-state write (closing the
viewer) fell inside the 500ms debounce, so the successor restored the
viewer open on page 2. The bar then carries no indicator to click, and
readDiagnostics read that as no messages. The act was read as running
all along (daemon.log: 'apply-update: act 1 is running; watching it').

test(colour): no dial position is exempt from parting neighbours, now that muted deals two tones (candybar-joiners-e5r4.tx7)

The grouped-row adjacency test and the door/rate test were written while
`muted` had one tone, so each named it as the one exemption and guarded
that it stayed the only one. With `muted` dealing its muted form and the
role itself, that state no longer exists: the guard now asserts no
position deals fewer than two tones, and both tests hold every position
to parting its neighbours, so a one-tone shade cannot come back unseen.
The theme-identity audit needed nothing: main's divider reversal already
removed its muted-row clause.

fix(colour): each distribution reads its placements by its own rule, so golden angle and the even spreads keep their promises (candybar-joiners-e5r4.tx7)

Whether two neighbours ever select one tone is a property of the pair
(distribution, rule), not of the window. Van der Corput keeps neighbours
apart only read by halves; golden angle only by equal bins (halves put
places 8 and 9 on one tone); and the even spreads ramp evenly in order
only by equal bins (halves dealt a five-option monotonic menu 0, 1, 2, 2,
2). No one rule serves both van der Corput's rung-at-a-time walk and
golden angle, so the rule moves from the dial's rows onto each
distribution, and the Shade quantize column, the QUANTIZE table and its
name type go. A row's hue reads the same selection; under every
distribution it picks what it picked before.

The bundled bar authors no distribution, so no rendered byte changes.

Also: a dial position's tones are two at least by type; the walk test
covers every window; the adjacency test states its scope (van der Corput
at every position, golden angle over three tones); the even spreads and
the activated rung are pinned; the authoring doc, design doc, memory and
audit comment stop saying a muted row is one colour or read to the
nearest point.

fix(colour): adjacent row positions never select one tone, and the muted dial gets two (candybar-joiners-e5r4.tx7)

A three-tone window is read by halves instead of by nearest point: the
upper half of the circle is the window's last entry (its middle rung) and
the lower half is split the same way between its ends. Van der Corput's
first bit is the index's parity, so every odd place wears the middle rung
and the even places alternate low and high. Of two neighbours exactly one
is odd, so no two neighbours share a tone at any index, and every step is
one rung. Nearest point centred a tone on 0, where places 2^k - 1 and 2^k
land either side ever closer, so 7 and 8, 15 and 16, ... shared it.

The muted position deals the role's muted form and the role itself, read
by bin, so its neighbours alternate too.

One property test states it for every dial position over rows of 2 to 16
cells; it replaces the adjacency checks that were spread over three tests.
The 🧪 toggles row's eighth item moves from the low rung to the middle one.

fix(colour): grouped cells and the door's rate cell take their own row positions (candybar-joiners-e5r4.3m7) (#493)

* fix(colour): grouped cells and the door's rate cell take their own row positions (candybar-joiners-e5r4.3m7)

A container inside a row was one address, so every cell in it wore one
shade: a grouped { h } drew in one colour, and so did the settings door
and its frame-rate cell. The compile now places every leaf of a row at
its own place on the row's line, through any nested { h }, and stores
each child's step on its container; a cell is read as its innermost cell
step. A { v } in a row draws its first child on the row's line and each
other on a line of its own below, each placed from where it sits.

Edit chrome's unit around a content cell is marked `unit` (synthesis-
only) and shares the cell's one place, so edit mode recolours nothing.
The loader refuses a distribution anywhere inside a row with one
message. Snapshots and doc render fences regenerate: the door's divider
becomes an arrow and the cells after it move one place.

* fix(colour): every drawn line's ends wear its keystones, and a gated first row's distribution places its cells (candybar-joiners-e5r4.3m7)

A `{ v }` inside a row draws lines below the row whose places count from
where the `{ v }` sits, and the row's count is the farthest place any line
reaches. Keystones read `count - 1` as the line's end, so the row line's last
leaf lost line-end whenever a lower line reached further, and a lower line's
first leaf never wore line-start. Every address step now carries the first
and last place of the line its node is drawn on; the keystones read those,
and the region memo compares them.

The default door placement wraps a gated first row in a new row after
cross-ref has accepted the gated row's `distribution`. Nested in that row,
it placed nothing, and the author's distribution was ignored without a word.
The wrapper now carries it, so a gated first row places its cells as an
ungated one does.

Tests: a `{ v }` in a row (the lines it draws, every leaf's place and the
row's count, each line's keystones, a count-reading distribution);
a gated first row; the `muted` exemption named and guarded so it cannot
widen and fails once that position gains a second tone; hiding through a
group nested two deep.

* docs(colour): the colour design doc states that a row's leaves take its places, edit chrome's unit excepted (candybar-joiners-e5r4.3m7)

The rule and two Decisions bullets still said anything nested inside a cell
wears the cell's colour. They now state the leaf rule, and a 3m7 entry in
Decisions says why grouping is layout, what a `{ v }` in a row places, why
the keystones read line ends rather than the count, and why edit chrome's
unit shares one place and is a mark on a container rather than a node kind.

* fix(colour): a `{ v }` whose first child draws nothing gives its line to the next, and a gated row's distribution moves to the row that leads it (candybar-joiners-e5r4.3m7)

A vertical container's first line is drawn by the first child that draws a
line, since an empty container draws none. Placement took the first child's
width whatever it was, so in `[a, { v: [{ h: [] }, b] }, c]` b and c drew
side by side at one place, in one shade, with a divider between them. A
child of a vertical container now starts a line of its own only once an
earlier child has drawn one, and a container's width is the places of the
children on its first line; the empty-container fallback goes with it.

The door placement now moves a gated row's distribution onto the row it
builds around it, rather than copying it, so the synthesized tree has one
placer per row and no distribution inside a row, as the loader requires of
an authored one.

`placeChildren` loses its export: the compile is its only caller. The
comment on `distribution` says where it is read and what count a
count-reading distribution reads.

* refactor(colour): a line's width is named once, and a gated row keeps its row and moves only its gate in (candybar-joiners-e5r4.3m7)

A container's width and a row's line end now read one `widthOf` beside
`reachOf`, over the children already laid out, instead of laying the row
out a second time to ask its span.

The door placement led a gated row by building a new row and moving the
distribution onto it, one field picked by hand. A field that only a row
reads, added later, would have stayed on the inner node and been ignored.
Now the gated row stays the row and only its gate moves in, onto a
container around its cells, so whatever makes it a row stays where a row
is read.

* test(colour): the bar's bytes give the rate cell its own place over the named activated shades (candybar-joiners-e5r4.3m7)

test(watchers): the unreadable-folder test skips under root, which ignores directory permissions (brandon-unfiled-3248.0mvx)

fix(watchers): the registry refuses a directory it cannot open, on every platform (brandon-unfiled-3248.0mvx)

On Node 20 and 22, Linux's recursive fs.watch is Node's own walk, and its
start swallows every error but ENOENT: a tree behind a symlink loop or an
unreadable folder came back as a watch that never fires, held as listening.
The registry now opens every directory before it watches it, so the open's
error is the refusal's reason whatever the platform or Node.

The git cache's ELOOP test asserts exactly two refusals instead of the
platform's count, and the registry suite pins an unreadable folder refused
as a tree or not.
